name: PixiTween Director S04: Muse Image plates + SAM cut-out layers
description: The five art tools (generatePlate, replacePlate, placeProduct, addSubject, setHeadlineBehindProduct) and their pure helpers: prompt lint, placement maths, SAM cut-out pipeline, plate generation and crop, role-ordered layer upsert. Offline only: Muse Image and SAM are faked with makeFakeMeta and the seed fixtures. Deliberately leaves out the director agent (S3b), self-review (S5), generate-mode clips (S7) and any engine change.

userStories.title: Art errors, prices and event helpers
userStories.description: As a tool author, I want shared error, price and event helpers so that every art tool reports failures, costs and assets the same way.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-04-muse-image-sam-layers/design.md sections 7 and 8, shared/tools.ts (ToolCtx, ToolResult), shared/events.ts (art.asset, cost, error) and server/ledger.ts.

Create server/art/errors.ts exporting type ArtErrorCode = 'no-object' | 'alpha-size-mismatch' | 'bad-image' | 'too-large' | 'order-invalid' | 'unknown-scene' | 'lint' | 'generate-mode' | 'plate-exists' | 'no-plate' and class ArtError extends Error { constructor(readonly code: ArtErrorCode, message: string) }, plus toolError(e: unknown): { ok: false; error: string } that returns ArtError messages as-is and 'internal error' (no stack) for anything else.
Create server/art/prices.ts exporting const PRICE = { museImageUsd: 0.01, samImageUsd: 0.0025 } as const.

Create server/art/events.ts exporting emitAsset(ctx: ToolCtx, asset: AssetRef) (emits { type:'art.asset', filmId: ctx.filmId, at: new Date().toISOString(), asset }) and charge(ctx: ToolCtx, model: string, units: string, usd: number) (calls ctx.ledger.add(ctx.filmId, model, units, usd) once).
Create server/art/errors.test.ts and server/art/events.test.ts using makeTestFilm from server/test-utils/film.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: toolError(new ArtError('no-object','no mug found in the photo')) returns { ok:false, error:'no mug found in the photo' }
toolError(new Error('boom at /secret/path')) returns { ok:false, error:'internal error' } and the result contains no 'boom' and no path
emitAsset pushes exactly one event with type 'art.asset', the film id and an ISO-8601 'at' string into makeTestFilm().events
charge(ctx,'sam-3.1','1 image',PRICE.samImageUsd) increases ctx.ledger.total(ctx.filmId) by 0.0025
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Prompt lint: brand names and named people
userStories.description: As a safety-minded owner, I want image prompts linted before they are sent so that no real brand or real person is requested from Muse Image.
steps: Read design.md section 6.2 and docs/hackathon/steps/step-01-meta-api-probes/findings.md (U-3 transcript example).

Create server/art/lint.ts exporting DENYLIST (at least 30 lower-case well-known marks including 'nike', 'adidas', 'coca-cola', 'pepsi', 'starbucks', 'iphone', 'macbook', 'samsung', 'sony', 'ikea', 'lego', 'disney', 'netflix', 'tesla', 'gucci', 'rolex', 'red bull'; do NOT include common words such as 'apple').

Export lintPrompt(prompt: string, opts?: { brandTerms?: string[]; subject?: boolean }): { ok: boolean; violations: Array<{ rule: 'brand-name' | 'named-person'; term: string }> }: whole-word, case-insensitive brand match against DENYLIST plus opts.brandTerms; when opts.subject is true also flag 'named-person' for two consecutive capitalised words that are not a brand term and for the phrases 'looks like', 'resembling', 'likeness of', 'celebrity', 'famous actor'.

Export extractBrandTerms(text: string): string[]: capitalised word sequences (3+ letters, optional trailing 'Co'-style suffix word) that are not at the start of a sentence, minus a stop-list of common capitalised words; trailing periods are stripped.
Create server/art/lint.test.ts with the cases in the acceptance criteria.
acceptanceCriteria: lintPrompt('A Nike shoe on a table') returns ok:false with violations [{ rule:'brand-name', term:'nike' }]
lintPrompt('warm oak counter at sunrise. No people.') returns ok:true with an empty violations array
lintPrompt('an apple orchard at dawn') returns ok:true (the word 'apple' is not denylisted)
extractBrandTerms("it's our our new cold brew from Coffee Co. I want a 22nd film of a white a white mug") returns exactly ['Coffee Co']
lintPrompt('Coffee Co mug', { brandTerms: ['Coffee Co'] }) returns ok:false with term 'coffee co'
lintPrompt('Portrait of Tom Hanks', { subject: true }) returns a violation with rule 'named-person'; the same prompt without subject:true returns ok:true
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Placement maths: trimBox, coverBox, productBox
userStories.description: As an art-pipeline author, I want pure placement functions so that cut-outs and plates are positioned the same way every time.
steps: Read design.md sections 5.2 and 5.4 (formulas and worked examples).

Create server/art/geometry.ts exporting type Box = { left:number; top:number; right:number; bottom:number }, type Rect = { x:number; y:number; w:number; h:number }, trimBox(bounds: Box, imgW: number, imgH: number): Box, coverBox(img: {w:number;h:number}, comp: {w:number;h:number}, overscan?: number): Rect and productBox(img, comp, opts?: { heightFrac?: number; cx?: number; baseline?: number }): Rect with the defaults heightFrac 0.6, cx 0.5, baseline 0.82.

trimBox grows bounds by m = max(2, round(0.01 * max(width, height))) on every side and clamps to [0,imgW] x [0,imgH]. productBox caps the width at 0.8 * comp.w and recomputes the height from the aspect ratio.
Create server/art/geometry.test.ts with the numeric cases below.
acceptanceCriteria: trimBox({left:180,top:705,right:702,bottom:1137}, 768, 1344) returns {left:175,top:700,right:707,bottom:1142}
trimBox({left:725,top:599,right:1338,bottom:1101}, 1920, 1280) returns {left:719,top:593,right:1344,bottom:1107}
trimBox({left:0,top:0,right:100,bottom:50}, 100, 50) returns {left:0,top:0,right:100,bottom:50} (clamped)
productBox({w:532,h:442},{w:1080,h:1920}) is within 0.05 of {x:108,y:856.6,w:864,h:717.8} (width cap applied)

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)

userStories.title: Layer helpers: inner assets, mask meta, camera re-apply
userStories.description: As a tool author, I want small pure helpers over the composition so that art tools satisfy the engine's per-composition asset rule and keep camera motion.
steps: Read design.md sections 4.4, 5.9 and 11 (V-6), contract-issues.md, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 4a (addLayer copies the asset into the scene precomp; setCamera is idempotent) and section 3a (meta.director.productNoun), and server/authoring/api.ts (S3a).

Create server/art/layers.ts exporting ROLE_RANK = ['bg','subject','product','headline','caption'] as const, ROLE_Z = { bg:10, subject:5, headline:3, product:1, caption:0 }, ensureInnerAsset(comp, sceneId, assetId) (a defensive guard: structuredClone; copies comp.assets[assetId] into comp.precomps[sceneId].assets only if it is missing, so it is a no-op when addLayer already copied it; idempotent; throws ArtError('unknown-scene') or a plain Error naming the asset when either is absent), withMaskAsset(comp, layerId, maskAssetId) (sets meta.director.layers[layerId].maskAssetId on a clone; throws when the layer is unknown), withProductNoun(comp, noun) (sets meta.director.productNoun on a clone) and reapplyCamera(comp, film: FilmState, sceneId) (move = film.storyboard?.scenes.find(s => s.id === sceneId)?.camera ?? 'static'; returns setCamera(comp, sceneId, move)).
Create server/art/layers.test.ts that builds a film with newFilmComposition, addScene, registerAsset and addLayer from server/authoring/api.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: After registerAsset + addLayer of an image layer (which already copies the asset into precomps.s1.assets per the amended 4a), ensureInnerAsset(comp,'s1',assetId) returns a deep-equal composition (a no-op) that passes parseAepCompositionSafe; after deleting precomps.s1.assets[assetId] from a clone, ensureInnerAsset restores it and the composition validates again
ensureInnerAsset is idempotent: calling it twice returns deep-equal compositions, and the input composition is never mutated (compare with a structuredClone taken before the call)

withMaskAsset(comp,'s1:product','mask_1').meta.director.layers['s1:product'].maskAssetId === 'mask_1'; an unknown layer id throws; withProductNoun(comp,'mug').meta.director.productNoun === 'mug' and the input is not mutated
reapplyCamera with a storyboard camera 'dolly-in' called twice yields deep-equal compositions (idempotency of setCamera); with no storyboard it applies 'static'

userStories.title: replaceRoleLayer: upsert keeping z-order and opacity
userStories.description: As a tool author, I want to replace or add a role layer without disturbing the rest of the scene so that art tools never reshuffle what the director built.
steps: Read design.md section 5.8 and 5.5, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 4a (the amended box semantics: x,y top-left, position = (x+w/2, y+h/2), anchor = (assetW/2, assetH/2), scale = (w/assetW, h/assetH)), and server/authoring/api.ts (addLayer, removeLayer, reorderLayer, layerIdsByRole).

In server/art/layers.ts add replaceRoleLayer(comp, sceneId, role, spec: Parameters<typeof addLayer>[1], opts?: { keepOpacity?: boolean }): Comp. When an old layer exists: remember the layer immediately below it and its transform.opacity, removeLayer(old), addLayer(spec), then reorderLayer(new,'back') if nothing was below else { above: prevId }, then copy the opacity value or keyframes onto the new layer on a clone. For role 'bg' the result is always index 0. When no old layer exists insert by ROLE_RANK: directly above the highest layer whose role rank is lower.

Add a test helper displayedRect(layerJson, assetJson) to server/art/test-support.ts returning { x, y, w, h } from transform.position, anchor, scale and the asset size (x = position.x - anchor.x*scale.x, w = assetW*scale.x, the same for y/h).
Extend server/art/layers.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: With scene layers [bg, product(raw photo), headline], replaceRoleLayer(...,'product', newSpec) yields the id order [s1:bg, s1:product, s1:headline] and the new layer references the new assetId
An old product layer with opacity keyframes [{t:0,v:0},{t:15,v:1}] passes them to the replacement unchanged
Adding a 'subject' to [bg, product, headline] yields [bg, subject, product, headline]; adding a 'caption' puts it last; replacing 'bg' always yields index 0

For addLayer box {x:570.05,y:237.6,w:779.9,h:648} on a 532x442 asset, displayedRect of the emitted layer equals that box within 0.5 px (pins the amended 4a contract: fails loudly if S3a's addLayer deviates)
The input composition is not mutated and the result passes parseAepCompositionSafe

userStories.title: Tool replacePlate
userStories.description: As a chat agent, I want replacePlate so that a scene's background can be regenerated without touching other layers.
steps: Read design.md sections 5.6, 5.8, 5.9 and 7 and the generatePlate tool in server/tools/art.ts.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.

Compose and edit the film only through the section 4a authoring API plus the documented pure JSON helpers in server/art/layers.ts (ensureInnerAsset, withMaskAsset, withProductNoun, opacity carry-over). Never write composition JSON by hand elsewhere.
Muse Image never receives a text-only prompt for the product: placeProduct has no image.generate path (test-enforced).

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner runs `npm run live -- s04-art` (prints the estimate), then `npm run live -- s04-art --yes` (about $0.08 expected, $0.30 ceiling): 2 scenes with plate, product cut-out and a subject. Check edges at 200 percent (no halo), product identity vs the photo, the Muse sizes returned (design U-1), then load the saved composition.json in the Player for parallax and text-behind-product.
